findings.title: Missing prisma import causes runtime crash
findings.body: File packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts calls prisma.credential.update at line 96 but never imports prisma. Any instantiation of SalesforceCalendarService will throw ReferenceError: prisma is not defined, breaking all Salesforce calendar operations after this PR.

findings.title: Stores Zod SafeParse wrapper as credential key
findings.body: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts the code does const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...) and then saves key directly as the credential key. parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the SafeParse result object { success, data/error }, not the parsed tokens. The DB will contain { success:true, data:{...} } instead of tokens, so subsequent googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) will fail and calendar calls break. Other services correctly use .data.

findings.title: Minimum token schema does not allow arbitrary keys
findings.body: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts the minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys like [z.string().toString()] which evaluates to a literal string such as ZodString, not a wildcard. Zod object defaults to stripping unknown keys, so expiry_date, expires_in, refresh_token etc. are stripped from data. When credential sharing is enabled this causes loss of expiry/refresh data and downstream credential corruption.

findings.title: Injects dummy refresh_token overwriting real token
findings.body: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts if the refresh response has no refresh_token the code sets data.refresh_token to the literal string refresh_token. Callers then persist this (Google, Office365 spread, Zoom/Webex assignment). This overwrites a valid stored refresh_token with a dummy value, permanently breaking future refreshes and hiding the fact the provider did not rotate the token.

findings.title: External branch returns fetch Response mismatching callers
findings.body: In packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts the sharing-enabled branch returns a raw fetch Response, while the fallback returns whatever refreshFunction returns. Google expects res.data, Hubspot expects a HubspotToken object with accessToken/expiresIn, Zoho Bigin/CRM expect an axios response with .data. A fetch Response has no .data, so Google gets undefined tokens, Hubspot computes NaN expiry, Zoho throws cannot read property error of undefined. No json parsing or response.ok check is done.

findings.title: Webhook allows any method and crashes on bad input
findings.body: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts the handler has no HTTP method check, so GET/PUT can create/update credentials. It calls zod parse, symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse without try/catch, so invalid body, wrong encryption key, or malformed JSON throws unhandled and returns 500 instead of 400. This exposes stack behavior and makes integration debugging unreliable for a credential-writing endpoint.

findings.title: Refreshed Salesforce token never used for connection
findings.body: In packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts getClient fetches a new access token and saves it, but then constructs jsforce.Connection with the old credentialKey.instance_url/access_token/refresh_token instead of the parsed refreshed values. The refresh is wasted and subsequent API calls continue using the expired token.

findings.title: Salesforce refresh checks statusText instead of ok
findings.body: In packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts the code throws if response.statusText !== OK. statusText is implementation-dependent and may be empty in fetch polyfills, causing false failures or missed HTTP errors. It should check response.ok or status code.

findings.title: Passes credentialId as userId to sync endpoint
findings.body: In packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts refreshAccessToken calls refreshOAuthTokens with credentialId as the third userId argument. The helper sends it as calcomUserId to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, so the external service receives a credential ID instead of a user ID and will look up the wrong user or fail.

findings.title: Wrong appSlug sent for Zoom refresh sync
findings.body: In packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts the refresh calls refreshOAuthTokens with appSlug zoomvideo, but the app is stored as appId zoom in the callback and credential. The external credential-sync endpoint receiving zoomvideo will not match the real slug zoom, so synced refresh will fail to resolve the user app.
